data.label: Provision a Stellar grant for a client
Create the client folder in Drive
Copy the blank grant template into the new folder
Create the grant_submission pipeline entity (state of record)
Link the folder + grant doc onto the client entity
Link the submission to the client (submitted_by) so graph.relations can find it
Only link a round when the trigger payload carries roundEntityId
Link the submission to its funding round (submitted_to)

metadata.purpose: Per-client grant provisioning as an AUTOMATION composing declarative Drive verbs: create a folder named for the client, copy the blank grant template into it (renamed 'stellar grant - {client}'), create the `grant_submission` PIPELINE entity (the durable state of record — stage 'scope') for the copied doc, link the Drive URLs onto the client entity, and link the submission to the client via `submitted_by` (and, when the payload carries roundEntityId, to its funding round via `submitted_to`) so it is discoverable by graph.relations (the proactive-grant-review automation reads the submitted_by edge). The Drive doc stays an attached link (submission.sourceSubmissionUrl), NOT the pipeline identity. Run per client with a manual trigger payload { client, clientEntityId, roundEntityId? }.
prerequisites: verbs `drive_create_folder` + `drive_copy_file` seeded from the nango-google capability (declarative Drive writes), and the `graph.link` verb seeded (internal graph write).

a connected Google account (nango-google) — set each Drive capability node's connectionSelector.connectionId (bridge-setup fills this at seed time). The `graph.link` node needs NO connection (internal pod verb).

automation.state must carry `clientsFolderId` (the shared 'clients' parent folder — prefilled) and `grantTemplateFileId` (the blank grant template's Drive FILE id — replace the placeholder; find it with drive_search inside the template folder).

GRANT_SUBMISSION PROFILE: the pipeline record is a first-class `grant_submission` entity (seeded by the `grants` workspace template — grants.yaml). Its `stage`/`status`/`outcome` enums drive the kanban Pipeline view; the Drive doc URL is captured as `sourceSubmissionUrl` (an attached link, not the identity). dedupeBy `sourceRecordId` (stamped with the client entity id) makes re-provisioning idempotent — a re-run for the same client reuses the existing submission — AND lets the daily Client Sync (which also dedupes grant_submission on sourceRecordId) reuse THIS same submission rather than create a second. NOTE: the Drive folder/copy verbs run BEFORE the entity dedupe, so a manual re-run still creates duplicate Drive artifacts (a resolve-or-create-folder guard is a follow-up); only the pipeline entity is deduped here. entity_create is proposal-gated — {{steps.create-dossier.output.entityId}} resolves once the write is applied; if your engine defers creation, apply the proposal before the link. The client entity should define `grantFolderUrl` + `grantDocUrl` so the link-to-client entity_update lands cleanly.

RELATION TYPES: `submitted_by` (grant_submission -> company) and `submitted_to` (grant_submission -> round) are the grants.yaml entityLinks. `proactive-grant-review.automation.json` resolves the submission via graph.relations(relationType:'submitted_by', direction:'inbound') on the client — keep both in sync.

trigger payload per run: { client: string, clientEntityId: uuid, roundEntityId?: uuid }. When roundEntityId is present the round-gate condition fires the submitted_to link; when absent it is skipped (no broken link). Follow-up (not in this template): an AI fill/judge verb that docs_get the grant, reads other clients' captured grant data for pre-fill, and writes back — governed via checkPermissionOrPropose.
